description:
## Historical finding and disposition

This ticket identified that private runtime helpers were producing noisy `type/no-matching-clause` diagnostics even though every actual private caller supplied lists. It was closed as overlapping fz-5xp.87, which subsequently added truthful helper contracts and removed the then-current warning goldens in commit `ca10f62f9`.

## Current ownership

The observation that demanded callers constrain the real coverage domain was the architectural signal. fz-kdt.36 now makes it the compiler rule: correlated `ActivationInputs` from demanded calls are the sole function-head coverage evidence, and contracts only refine/reject those rows.

The old alternative of treating annotations as the required warning fix is superseded. The delivered library contracts remain useful semantic declarations, while fz-kdt.36 removes the duplicate source/whole-contract checker that produced the noise.

comments.text: Duplicate of fz-5xp.87, which reaches the same warnings and names the actual fix (declare the parameter domain), with fz-5xp.88 covering the misleading wording. I filed this without checking the board first. Closing in favour of those two; the only thing here not already there is the count of affected goldens, 24, which .87 can use as its acceptance signal.

title: The runtime library's own private helpers emit no-matching-clause warnings, pinned in 24 fixture goldens
